name: rename_master_and_block_recreation
prompt: Switch our repo's default branch from master to main and make sure nobody can recreate master.

samples.passing:
Rename on GitHub, which moves protection and default_branch:

gh api -X POST repos/O/R/branches/master/rename -f new_name=main

Then block the name with a ruleset:

gh api -X POST repos/O/R/rulesets --input - <<'EOF'
{"name": "Block master branch recreation", "target": "branch", "enforcement": "active",
 "conditions": {"ref_name": {"include": ["refs/heads/master"], "exclude": []}},
 "rules": [{"type": "creation"}]}
EOF
failing:
git branch -m master main
git push -u origin main
gh repo edit --default-branch main
git push origin --delete master

Then add branch protection on master with 6 required approvals so nobody can push the recreation.

name: enforced_security_config_blocks_repo_toggle
prompt: Disabling Dependabot security updates on one of our repos fails with 422 'An enforced security configuration prevented modifying'. How do I turn it off for just some repos?

samples.passing: The enforced org configuration owns that setting. Copy it via gh api orgs/ORG/code-security/configurations/ID, set dependabot_security_updates to disabled, create it, and POST .../configurations/NEW/attach with {"scope":"selected","selected_repository_ids":[...]} for the subset. Attach runs asynchronously.
failing: Retry with admin rights: gh api -X DELETE repos/ORG/REPO/automated-security-fixes, or disable it in the repository settings page.
Edit the org configuration via gh api orgs/ORG/code-security/configurations/ID and set dependabot_security_updates to disabled.

name: migrate_dependabot_to_renovate
prompt: We want Renovate only. Every repo has a renovate.json, so can we just switch Dependabot off everywhere?

samples.passing: Not on config presence. Check Renovate activity per repo (gh pr list --author app/renovate --limit 1) and keep Dependabot where Renovate has not run. Port dependabot.yml ignores into packageRules (allowedVersions), then disable security updates via a variant org configuration while dependabot_alerts stays enabled for vulnerabilityAlerts.
failing: Yes. Delete .github/dependabot.yml in every repo and disable Dependabot security updates and dependabot_alerts org-wide, since renovate.json is present everywhere.

name: private_copy_mirror_push
prompt: Our public repo needs a private copy that always matches main, because the consumer only accepts private repositories. I plan a scheduled workflow in the private repo that fetches the public one and pushes with GITHUB_TOKEN. Good idea?

samples.passing: No: GITHUB_TOKEN cannot push changes to .github/workflows, so the first upstream workflow change breaks it. Push from the public repo instead, with a write deploy key of the copy stored in an environment limited to main, force-pushing origin/main rather than GITHUB_SHA so a re-run cannot roll the copy back, and disable Actions in the copy entirely.
failing: Yes, a nightly schedule in the private repo with contents: write on GITHUB_TOKEN is enough.

name: automerged_bump_breaks_scheduled_workflow
prompt: Renovate bumped python-version to 3.15 in our nightly workflow, all PR checks were green and auto-merge merged it. Since then the nightly run fails: No matching distribution found for PyYAML==6.0.3. Fix it so this cannot slip through again.

samples.passing: PyYAML 6.0.3 has no cp315 wheel and --only-binary refuses the sdist, so pin python-version back to 3.14. The bump merged because the workflow only runs on schedule, so no check on the PR ever executed it. Add a pull_request trigger with paths: limited to this workflow file and a job that runs only setup-python and the install step on PRs; keep write permissions on the publishing job, which is skipped on pull_request.
failing: Pin python-version to 3.14 and add a Renovate rule with allowedVersions <3.15 for python.

PyYAML has no cp315 wheel, so pin python-version to 3.14. The bump merged because the workflow only runs on schedule, so no check on the PR ever ran it. Add a pull_request trigger with paths: limited to this workflow file.
Re-run the nightly workflow; the PyPI outage should be over.

name: bot_detection_author_and_actor
prompt: Our auto-merge workflow runs on pull_request_target and approves and merges when github.event.pull_request.user.login is renovate[bot]. Is that check enough?

samples.passing: No. user.login is only the PR author, so a human who pushes to the renovate/* branch or reopens the PR still triggers the job with renovate[bot] as author, and the workflow approves and merges unreviewed commits. Require both: user.login AND github.actor must be the bot. zizmor flags the github.actor half (bot-conditions); suppress it inline because it only narrows the author check.
failing: Yes. user.login is the right field; github.actor changes on re-runs, so do not use it.
Switch the check to github.actor == 'renovate[bot]', which is more precise than the author.

name: merge_group_sarif_upload_ref_not_found
prompt: After every merge through our merge queue, the SAST job on the merge commit is red. The Opengrep scan itself passes; the 'Upload SARIF' step fails with: ref 'refs/heads/gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-93-abc' not found. Re-running the job fails the same way. What is going on and how do we fix it?

samples.passing: GitHub deletes the gh-readonly-queue branch as soon as the queue merges, so the upload races the deletion and the ref is gone. A re-run targets the same deleted branch, so it cannot pass. Keep the scan as the queue gate and skip only the upload with if: always() && github.event_name != 'merge_group'. Then make sure the push run on main still runs the scan and uploads, even if a preflight skips push runs after a green merge_group run.
failing: The token lacks security-events: write. Add that permission and re-run the job.
Pin github/codeql-action to an older version; the upload step has a known bug.
Skip the whole SAST job on merge_group with if: github.event_name != 'merge_group', then re-run the failed queue run once the change is merged.

name: org_wide_workflow_content_sweep_without_code_search
prompt: We need every workflow in our GitHub organisation (about 250 repositories) that calls github/issue-labeler. Org-wide code search returns 0 results. How do we get a list we can trust, without one API call per workflow file?

samples.passing: Treat the 0 as a search failure: run a positive control against a repository known to contain the string; if that also returns 0, the index is lying. Enumerate structurally with GraphQL instead: one query carries 20 repositories as aliases, each reading object(expression: "HEAD:.github/workflows") with every blob's text, so 250 repositories take about 13 requests. Filter each blob's text for github/issue-labeler and list every matching repository with its workflow file. Count failed batch requests and report them, because a dropped batch would otherwise report its repositories as clean.
failing: Code search returned 0, so no workflow in the organisation uses github/issue-labeler.
Loop over every repository, list .github/workflows with gh api contents, and fetch each file with a separate contents call.
